definitions.explanation: The period of youth and adolescence, typically the teenage years through early twenties. Carries a nostalgic and idealized connotation, evoking energy, passion, and formative experiences. Widely used in Japanese media, especially for stories about high school life.

examples.japanese: {青春|せいしゅん}を{楽|たの}しむ。
{部活|ぶかつ}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}んだ{日々|ひび}が、{私|わたし}の{青春|せいしゅん}だった。
examples.english: The days I devoted myself to club activities were my youth.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}{時代|じだい}は{二度|にど}と{戻|もど}らない{青春|せいしゅん}の{一|ひと}ページだから、{後悔|こうかい}のないように{過|す}ごしたい。
examples.english: High school is a page of one's youth that never comes back, so I want to live it without regrets.

notes:
USAGE:
{青春|せいしゅん} literally means "blue/green spring" and comes from Chinese philosophy where spring and the color blue/green represent youth. It has a strongly nostalgic and romanticized tone and is a staple of Japanese pop culture, especially in {青春|せいしゅん}ドラマ (youth dramas) and {青春|せいしゅん}{映画|えいが} (coming-of-age films).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {青春|せいしゅん}{時代|じだい} (one's youth; adolescent years)
- {青春|せいしゅん}を{捧|ささ}げる (to devote one's youth to)
- {青春|せいしゅん}ドラマ (youth drama)
- {青春|せいしゅん}{映画|えいが} (coming-of-age film)
- {青春|せいしゅん}の{思|おも}い{出|で} (memories of one's youth)
- {青春|せいしゅん}を{謳歌|おうか}する (to fully enjoy one's youth)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {青春|せいしゅん}: youth (nostalgic, idealized)
- {若|わか}さ: youthfulness (physical quality of being young)
- {思春期|ししゅんき}: puberty, adolescence (biological/developmental stage)
